claims.text: Defense Intelligence Reference Document titled "Antigravity for Aerospace Applications", series "Acquisition Threat Support", published 2010-03-30 with an Intelligence Cut-Off Date (ICOD) of 2009-12-01, DIA document number DIA-08-1003-018. Released by DIA under FOIA and posted in the DIA FOIA Electronic Reading Room.

Inside cover reads: "This product is one in a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2009 under the Defense Intelligence Agency [redacted b(3) 10 USC 424] Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program" and directs questions to the "AAWSA Program Manager, Defense Intelligence Agency, ATTN: [redacted], Bldg 6000, Washington, DC 20340-5100".

Author name is withheld in the DIA-released copy under FOIA exemption (b)(6); the "Prepared by:" line is withheld under (b)(3) 10 USC 424. The released cover therefore does not attribute the DIRD to a named author.
Released PDF is 44 pages, marked UNCLASSIFIED//FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY (FOUO caveat partially illegible in the scan).

claims.text: THE ZERO-COUNTS, taken over the whole released 45-page PDF on 19 September 2026: Biefeld 0, electrogravitics 0, ion wind 0, Podkletnov 0, and THOMAS TOWNSEND BROWN ABSENT. The three occurrences of 'Brown' are other authors' surnames in the reference list. Alcubierre occurs once, as reference [43], the 1994 Classical and Quantum Gravity citation, and that is its only appearance in this document. A count is checkable and an adjective is not, which is why the node carries numbers.

claims.text: Its contents page, as released: 'Concepts for Antigravity Within Newtonian Physics', 'Negating Newtonian Gravity', 'Energy Estimate for Newtonian Levitation', 'Concepts for Antigravity Within General Relativity', 'Antigravity via Gravitomagnetic Forces', 'Forward's Dipole Gravitational Field Generator', 'Felber's Relativistic Antigravity Effect', 'Negative Energy-Induced Antigravity', 'Cosmological Antigravity', 'Pressure as a Source of Gravity', 'Vacuum Energy of Einstein's Cosmological Constant', 'Dark Energy', 'Antigravity Propulsion Application of Dark/Vacuum Energy', 'Quantum Antigravity Propulsion Concepts', 'Antigravity via Quantum Vacuum Zero-Point Fluctuation Force', 'Antigravity via Nonretarded Quantum Interatomic Dispersion Force', 'Conclusion: The Way Forward', with appendices on static radial fields, squeezed quantum vacuum, gravitationally squeezed electromagnetic zero-point fluctuations and the dynamical Casimir effect.

claims.source: Defense Intelligence Reference Document DIA-08-1003-018, 'Antigravity for Aerospace Applications', 30 March 2010, ICOD 1 December 2009, 45 pages as released, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/documents/dia/AAWSAP-DIRDs/DIRD_19-DIRD_Antigravity_for_Aerospace_Applications.pdf , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: Its conclusion, 'The Way Forward', verbatim in part: 'This report has reviewed and analyzed a number of antigravity concepts that are found within Newtonian gravity theory, General Relativity Theory, semi-classical quantum gravity theory, quantum field theory, and nonretarded quantum interatomic dispersion force theory. One found that plausible mechanisms exist within Newtonian and general relativistic theories whereby one could embody a realistic device that produces a significant antigravity force. However, one discovered that there are daunting technical challenges that arise in each of the proposed embodiments.'

claims.source: Defense Intelligence Reference Document DIA-08-1003-018, 'Antigravity for Aerospace Applications', 30 March 2010, ICOD 1 December 2009, 45 pages as released, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/documents/dia/AAWSAP-DIRDs/DIRD_19-DIRD_Antigravity_for_Aerospace_Applications.pdf , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: And: 'Antigravity forces produced by quantum electromagnetic vacuum ZPF or by nonretarded quantum interatomic dispersion forces in a curved spacetime (that is, gravitational field) are very feeble, but there are proposals based on other theoretical and empirical studies which suggest that these forces can be amplified to macroscopic level. However, there are a number of difficult technical challenges to overcome in order to achieve success.' Its first named next step is that 'Presently, the technology does not exist to achieve the astronomical mass densities, extreme velocities or accelerations of mass motion, and the large device dimensions required to produce large enough antigravity forces for useful propulsion'.
Authored by Dr Eric Davis of EarthTech International, per the 9 January 2018 DIA list (item 11).
Cover page reads "30 March 2010 / ICOD: 1 December 2009 / DIA-08-1003-018", series "Acquisition Threat Support".

WHAT THIS IS NOT: a finding that DIA considered Brown and rejected him, because the document shows no sign of having considered him. dossier.narrative:
The popular account of antigravity research has a founding figure. Thomas Townsend Brown, his two patents, and the electrogravitics literature of the 1950s are treated as the origin of the whole subject, and this board carries them because the account carries them.

This document is what happens when the government surveys the same field. Over the complete released 45-page PDF, taken on 19 September 2026: **Biefeld 0, electrogravitics 0, ion wind 0, Podkletnov 0, and Thomas Townsend Brown absent entirely.** The three occurrences of the string 'Brown' are other authors' surnames in the reference list.

What is in it instead is its own contents page: 'Concepts for Antigravity Within Newtonian Physics', 'Negating Newtonian Gravity', 'Energy Estimate for Newtonian Levitation', and the corresponding treatment within general relativity. It is a physics review, and it reaches for the physics rather than for the lore.

The careful statement of what this proves, and it is narrower than it first looks: a survey's silence is evidence about the survey, not proof that a subject is empty. What it establishes is that when a defence intelligence agency paid for a literature review of antigravity in 2009, the reviewer did not consider Brown worth a sentence. That is a fact about how the documented research community regards the man the lore treats as its founder, and the board carries it as exactly that and no more.

dossier.whyImplicated: It is the United States government's own survey of antigravity, commissioned by a defence intelligence agency, and it is the single best control document this board carries for the propulsion strand. What a government study of a subject contains is evidence. What it does not contain is evidence too, and this one does not contain the thing the lore says is at its centre.
